concerns: Last-save persistence across plugin process Stop/Activate still depends on the in-memory mapping store from T-map-resolve; a new Service does not reload mappings. This UI reloads the last save from the live service on page refresh and handler reconstruction. Host-side sidebar mounting remains out of this repo's scope.
execution.summary: cloudflare-dns now serves a dedicated mapping admin page and JSON API from the live Service (Controller.ServeHTTP mounts it when a generation is active). Authorized admins can create, rename, rotate, and delete suffix mappings; refresh and handler reconstruction on the live service return the last successful save. Token fields are write-only and never returned in list, detail, edit HTML, errors, or audit/UI traces. Unenrolled callers get an explicit 403 denial page instead of a blank body, and read-only callers see no write controls. Delete, rotate, and rename require a matching confirm; cancel or a missing/mismatched confirm leaves mappings unchanged. Duplicate normalized suffixes still return conflict. The page does not add DNS record CRUD, zone-token fields, or ui.schema.json.

execution.summary: Fixed the T-mapping-ui review findings in plugins/cloudflare-dns. Absent X-NRE-Operation-Key now mints a unique per-gesture key, and sendJSON sends one, so a second rotate stores the new Token and long suffixes no longer exceed refPattern. Mapping catalog state is persisted: NewService reloads a provided catalog, Controller.activate supplies a Vault catalog when none is injected, and Close/NewService plus Stop then a new Activate keep the last successful save. Token-bearing forms use method=post. List, detail, edit HTML, errors, and audit still omit Token plaintext.

execution.summary: Catalog Load now fails closed unless Vault.Verify returns ErrMappingCatalogNotFound; a missing catalog is empty, any other Verify/Reveal error fails NewService/Activate. Save no longer Rotates when the catalog was not restored, so an unrestored instance cannot overwrite a durable catalog. Mapping writes persist inside applyAndPersist; a failed save rolls back the live mutation and retires the new suffix epoch so the next create binds a new Vault identity. Replay of a committed create also persists. Plugin UI vaults return the dedicated not-found for a missing catalog.

execution.summary: Rotate now Verifies the live Vault version before CAS, so a persist-failed rotate no longer leaves the next unique-key rotate on a stale expectedVersion. CreateMapping treats an Enroll-already-exists identity with an uncommitted new operation key as a leftover: it retires that epoch and retries the next Vault identity. Tests lock persist-fail then retry rotate, and NewService after a failed create persist can save the suffix again.
